purpose: Pin source identity and document the synthetic crime-economics evaluator plus a separate non-compensatory aggregate lawful-alternative viability contract.
claim_ceiling: Source blob pinning detects unreviewed byte drift only; it is not a signature or source-authenticity proof.
Rust tests verify selected implementation invariants only.
The independent verifier validates artifact structure and specific cross-scenario relationships only.
No causal crime-reduction effect, model calibration, real-world validity, robot safety qualification, or jurisdictional generalization is established.
All outcome-generating parameters have explicit synthetic-assumption labels; no parameter in the register is an empirically estimated local coefficient.
The zero-quality-work-effect scenario tests behavior when the assumed work effect is disabled; neither setting is an empirical effect estimate.
The viability fixture evaluates synthetic gates only; it is not evidence that a real population has viable lawful alternatives.
Viability status is not a criminal-risk, individual eligibility, legal compliance, or causal crime-reduction score.
Stats SA QLFS descriptive statistics and ILO measurement frameworks are not used as crime-effect coefficients or as justification for synthetic numeric gates.
One cohort failing a floor or a group-gap gate cannot be compensated by a high aggregate mean.

The viability measurement dictionary defines a proposed operationalization; it is not a validated instrument until reviewed with affected communities, labour/statistical experts, and jurisdiction-specific specialists.
Low/high fixture bounds are not statistical confidence intervals.
Opportunity coverage must not be operationalized as vacancy count alone; quality criteria and its target-population denominator must be pre-registered.

parameter_registry.limitation: Defines simulation size and observation window only; not a claim about any real community.
Cohorts are anonymous aggregate cells with no person records or inferred individual attributes.
Illustrative starting conditions, not local housing, food, utilities, or benefits-access measurements.
The rates are not estimates of actual crime, violence, victimization, or offending.
These multipliers are illustrative heterogeneity controls, not proof that socioeconomic status or group membership predicts individual behavior.

evidence_context_sources.title: Quarterly Labour Force Survey, Quarter 2 2026 — key findings
evidence_context_sources.relevance: Provides current national labour-market context and official definitions/series for employment and underutilisation.
evidence_context_sources.limitation: The 33.6% national unemployment statistic is not a causal crime estimate, a local pilot baseline, a parameter for the synthetic crime model, or evidence that unemployment predicts an individual.

evidence_context_sources.title: Decent Work Indicators — Concepts and Definitions
evidence_context_sources.relevance: Supports a multidimensional measurement design spanning earnings, work safety, stability/security, and social protection.
evidence_context_sources.limitation: A measurement framework does not validate this prototype's thresholds or supply causal effects on crime.

evidence_context_sources.title: The ILO Framework on the Measurement of Decent Work
evidence_context_sources.relevance: Context for structuring labour and decent-work indicators.
evidence_context_sources.limitation: Used for construct coverage only; not an empirical parameter source for the simulation.

evidence_context_sources.title: Governance, Public Safety and Justice Survey 2025/26 — Victims of Crime Release
evidence_context_sources.relevance: Latest national victimization survey release; distinguishes incident counts, affected households, and the share reporting some or all incidents to police.
evidence_context_sources.limitation: National descriptive survey estimates are not Johannesburg pilot data, a causal effect coefficient, or an individual risk signal. Incident counts, affected-household counts, and reporting proportions are distinct measures. Technical notes report 85.57% national response, 76.97% for Gauteng, 73.72% for the City of Johannesburg, and 67.54% for the City of Tshwane; four geographic areas were below the cited 80% minimum-acceptable response rate. Response rates are quality diagnostics, not significance tests or proof every estimate in a lower-response area is invalid. Empirical comparisons must retain survey design and weights, indicator definitions and denominators, time comparability, geographic fit, and estimate-specific uncertainty information where available. Table 41's 3% coefficients of variation apply to household housebreaking experience (43.1% in 2024/25; 46.0% in 2025/26), not the distinct 43.4% to 48.2% police-reporting proportion. These CVs and rounded differences alone do not establish statistical significance; these are descriptive context, not model inputs.

viability_measure_definitions.unit: fraction of the pre-registered eligible cohort
viability_measure_definitions.numerator: Eligible households whose locally specified essential basket is actually available, affordable under the declared affordability rule, and reliably delivered over the reference period.
viability_measure_definitions.denominator: All eligible household-equivalents observed or represented in the same cohort and reference period, including people who did not successfully use an inaccessible service.
viability_measure_definitions.required_data: Defined essentials basket; service availability and interruption; local price/cost burden; eligible population and reference period.
viability_measure_definitions.non_substitution_rule: Nominal enrollment, benefit eligibility, or a nearby facility does not by itself establish actual access.

viability_measure_definitions.unit: fraction of the pre-registered target population
viability_measure_definitions.numerator: Members for whom at least one attainable lawful work or productive-participation option satisfies the predeclared access, fair-pay, safety, stability, and skills/accessibility criteria.
viability_measure_definitions.denominator: The full pre-registered target population for the service-area study, not merely the number of posted vacancies or people who succeeded in applying.
viability_measure_definitions.required_data: Opportunity inventory; eligibility/access rules; pay, safety, stability and accessibility characteristics; transport/time barrier; reference period.
viability_measure_definitions.non_substitution_rule: Vacancy totals or job-placement counts cannot substitute for attainable, quality-qualified options.

viability_measure_definitions.unit: fraction of relevant opportunities meeting predeclared pay criteria
viability_measure_definitions.numerator: Relevant lawful opportunities that meet applicable legal pay obligations and a locally defined, publicly reviewable adequacy benchmark for the reference context.
viability_measure_definitions.denominator: All relevant opportunities in the pre-registered opportunity inventory with sufficient pay and hours information; missing pay data must be reported rather than assumed adequate.
viability_measure_definitions.required_data: Applicable legal pay rules; transparent adequacy benchmark; gross/net treatment; paid hours; deductions and documented uncertainty.
viability_measure_definitions.non_substitution_rule: Employment counts or median pay alone do not establish that the available opportunities meet the declared adequacy floor.

viability_measure_definitions.unit: fraction of relevant opportunities meeting applicable safety criteria
viability_measure_definitions.numerator: Relevant opportunities with evidence of satisfying applicable workplace safety duties and the study's declared worker-protection criteria.
viability_measure_definitions.denominator: All relevant opportunities assessed, with unassessed or missing safety information retained as unknown rather than passed.
viability_measure_definitions.required_data: Applicable jurisdiction-specific requirements; documented hazard controls; complaint/incident and inspection coverage; review period.
viability_measure_definitions.non_substitution_rule: An employer certificate or standards reference alone does not prove the work is safe in practice.

viability_measure_definitions.unit: fraction of relevant opportunities meeting predeclared stability criteria
viability_measure_definitions.numerator: Opportunities meeting the study's explicit thresholds for predictable hours/earnings and a declared minimum duration or continuity measure.
viability_measure_definitions.denominator: All relevant opportunities in the target inventory with sufficient contract, hours and duration data.
viability_measure_definitions.required_data: Declared stability definition; job tenure/contract type; volatility in hours and earnings; seasonal/temporary treatment; missing-data rate.
viability_measure_definitions.non_substitution_rule: A single snapshot of employment status cannot establish secure or stable work.

viability_measure_definitions.unit: fraction of eligible workers or opportunities with actual protection access
viability_measure_definitions.numerator: Eligible workers/opportunities for which the applicable protection exists and can practically be accessed under the declared scheme definition.
viability_measure_definitions.denominator: The population eligible for those protections under the applicable rules, with ineligible cases and unobserved eligibility reported separately.
viability_measure_definitions.required_data: Applicable scheme/rules; eligibility; registration and contribution status; claimability/access barriers; reference period.
viability_measure_definitions.non_substitution_rule: Formal entitlement or a registry entry alone does not establish effective access to benefits.

viability_measure_definitions.unit: minutes, with travel mode and statistic specified
viability_measure_definitions.numerator: A travel-time estimate to at least one opportunity that already satisfies the defined lawful-opportunity quality criteria.
viability_measure_definitions.denominator: The pre-registered target-area aggregate and reference period, with routes/options inaccessible to relevant participants excluded or separately flagged.
viability_measure_definitions.required_data: Travel mode; origin/accessibility assumptions; cost as well as time; p50/p90 or other declared statistic; temporal variability and safety/accessibility constraints.
viability_measure_definitions.non_substitution_rule: Fast access to a poor-quality, unsafe or unattainable vacancy cannot make lawful alternatives viable.

viability_uncertainty_semantics.low_high_values: Illustrative fixture bounds for sensitivity and gate testing, not estimated sampling confidence intervals, statistical credible intervals, or uncertainty calibrated to South African data.
viability_uncertainty_semantics.real_data_requirement: For an empirical pilot, pre-register the source, denominator, reference period, missingness and uncertainty method for each measure; distinguish sampling error, measurement error, model uncertainty and disagreement between sources.

viability_status_semantics.fixture_pass: Every synthetic gate is satisfied for a fixture; this is not a finding about a real population or a legal determination.
viability_status_semantics.fixture_fail: At least one synthetic minimum, cap or cross-cohort coverage-gap rule is clearly violated.
viability_status_semantics.fixture_indeterminate: Missing, stale, conflicted or overly broad/threshold-straddling evidence prevents a pass/fail finding.

non_compensatory_rules: Any clearly failed cohort floor vetoes scenario-level pass regardless of the cohort or population mean.
Fair pay, safe work, stability, and social protection are separate gates; opportunity count cannot compensate for a failure in any of them.
Conservative cohort coverage-gap rules are evaluated after per-cohort gate checks and cannot be averaged away.
Unusable evidence, source age above the declared synthetic limit, missing measurements, or a threshold-straddling interval never defaults to pass.
No person-level risk score, eligibility action, criminal propensity inference, or enforcement decision is generated.
